searchText: I mean starting a fight with lido may be creating an enemy out of your biggest validator though. Then again they were asked nicely and refused 😅 I mean as I understand it, you can even exit now and immediately withdraw when withdrawals are available. The issue will come when you want to exit staking only when withdrawals are available, that will cause you to be in the exit queue first if a lot of people exit at the same time. I do prefer that we don't go to a UASF. Preferably a censorship resistant solution comes available that allows validators to have plausible deniability that they do not know what transactions they included/excluded and therefore cannot be prosecuted. Looks like RocketPool is introducing some type of penalty system because of the fact node operators can send priority fees/mev to an arbitrary address (cheating on their minipool partners). https://github.com/rocket-pool/rocketpool-research/blob/master/Penalties/penalty-system.md It also looks like they will force node operators to run MEV-Boost and if they don't, they will be penalized. https://docs.rocketpool.net/guides/redstone/native-migration.html#set-up-mev-boost Holy crap 10% that’s 3.2 eth+ And there’s no time expiry for penalties so even 1 strike a year adds up to you losing 80% in 10 years 😅 By this measure couldn’t someone acquire 51% of rocketpool tokens. Penalize everyone 80%. Then keep most of it cause it goes to the staking pool? Assuming that was sufficient to take over the Oracle DAO, it's still the case I suppose that if each penalty can be issued only to an individual validator when it proposes a penalisable block, then it's kind of rate limited. It still seems overly punitive. Maybe they should just run their own mev-boost relayer in order to control the fee recipient directly. The requirement for mev-boost won't be active until there are relays that can provide robust and monitorable distributed access, and there are multiple relay vendors in place. Until then operators will only be penalized for setting a wrong fee recipient. No. Penalties are assessed and voted on by the odao which is a permissioned group of high profile, doxed folks. Just buying up rpl does not give that power. Even the pdao (which sets some protocol parameters like commission and collateral requirements) is weighted by effectively staked rpl (rpl that is actively collateralizing validators). Hey guys, any plans to deal with the OFAC censorship issue? Really worried PoS effectively kills ethereum's censorship resistance... I am hoping there is some sort of mitigation to this is the works, as it would make PoS a really bad idea in this reguard. PoW is not any different. A PoW miner can skip certain tx to include in a block as they wish Right but look at who controls miners vs who controls stake The big difference is it effectively hands over majority control to regulated entities I mean the other option is to not recognize it as a potential problem, but the issue there is once it becomes a problem it may be much more difficult to fix... Ethermine just blocked Toronto Cash and they are PoW still. well each minipool (each validator, right?) only proposes like 10 blocks a year so it's a big deal And AWS controls mining at the end as most computers are hosted in AWS. There is always a weak link in the system. The key is not to avoid a big player like lido, but to think if a big layer cheats or fails, will the system break? It’s OK to have temporary interruptions while the system readjust. I doubt PoS is worse than PoW in this aspect <@686695036733227017> what happened to the time estimates / boundaries on your projection page? was fun to watch them That was a weird action given that they are Austrian and that they don’t have to follow OFAC sanctions. A tiny chunk of pools use AWS FYI Also this is true Very good one against PoS Staking pools are financial businesses, and they are heavily regulated by the government. PoW pools aren’t So it’s ok to assume that in the future Ethereum will be controlled by governments, if the staking pool problem won’t be solved is the block producer maket thing going to go live right after the merge?
